answer: Reputation-weighted action throttle. Each identity’s allowed action rate is set by its verified track record, so a fresh identity starts at one action per long window. Attacker cost is the time-and-fee treadmill of building history across each clone; a sparrow cannot borrow the orchard’s standing. Every new identity also pays a full onboarding fee at a busy wharf before acting, so mass cloning multiplies fixed costs that legitimate slow starters amortize.
